messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV-cache spill/backpressure on hosted-multitenant-gptq-int8 route. Disk-spill-rate elevated, KV-resident-bytes jumping ~3.8x. Alert start 2026-03-16T02:00:00Z.

yuki: seeing 99th latency climb and streaming pauses. tagging oncall @samir. preliminary traces show long serialization timeouts when writing KV segments to disk.

samir: oncall. pulling recent rollouts. Notable: 01:56 UTC rollout 'gptq-compact-headers-v3' and continuous-batcher config changed token_merge=enabled, merge_window_ms=1200 at 01:57. Suspect interaction.

ops-raj: telemetry: KV-serialized-entry-size histogram shifted right; median up ~2.1x, p95 up 3.7x. Breakdown by serializer_format shows GPTQ variants produce larger entries under compact-headers-v3 due to per-layer offset table being expanded to 32-bit alignment. Combined with token_merge we concatenate more segments so overhead multiplies.

cs-lina: customers: several streaming integrations reported stalls and reconnects (CS-4510, CS-4514). One enterprise tenant saw partial transcript loss due to stalled stream. Sending customer ack now.

samir: mitigation plan: 1) toggle compact-headers-v3 off for gptq pools 2) disable token_merge temporarily 3) enable spill-throttler to shed long-running requests 4) raise KV-eviction aggressiveness for 20m. I'll run flag flips and routing changes.

ops-raj: note: spill-throttler is a new runtime flag that throttles requests that cause >X MB write in last Y seconds; it will return 429 for non-critical lower-tier requests. Good to protect premium sessions.

samir: executing commands now:
```bash
# disable header experiment
redwood-admin pool-config set --pool hosted-multitenant-gptq-int8 --compact_headers_v3 false
# disable token merge
redwood-admin runtime-config set --name token_merge --value false --routes hosted-multitenant-gptq-int8
# enable spill throttler (thresholds are MB/sec)
redwood-admin runtime set-feature --name spill_throttler --params '{"write_threshold":50,"window_s":30,"deny_tier":"standard"}' --pools hosted-multitenant-gptq-int8
# bump eviction
redwood-admin kv set-eviction --pool hosted-multitenant-gptq-int8 --threshold 0.30 --grace 1200
```

deploy-bot: config-change: compact_headers_v3=false by samir at 02:04 UTC. runtime-change applied.

perf-bot: metric-note: within 90s of header toggle, kv-serialized-entry-size p50 dropped 26%. disk-spill-rate decreased 72% over next 3 minutes.

sre-omar: monitoring tails. Paging backpressure largely cleared but we still see occasional blips for requests with prefix_len>1500 tokens. Those create many small segments that reconstitute into a huge write.

yuki: for immediate safety can we route extremely long-prefix requests to dedicated fp16 pools? Lower risk than throttling premium customers.

samir: proposing temporary rule: if prefix_len>1200 AND tenant_tier=premium then route to hosted-gptq-fp16-pool, else apply spill-throttler. Applying now.

ops-raj: please also record trace ids for a couple of affected requests to attach to RCA. Examples: trace-c3a8, trace-c3b9. Good reproducible cases with seq_len ~1800 and merged token windows.

samir: added routing rule:
redwood-admin routing add-rule --route hosted-multitenant-gptq-int8 --condition "prefix_len>1200 && tenant_tier==\"premium\"" --target-pool hosted-gptq-fp16 --ttl 3600

deploy-bot: routing-rule-added by samir at 02:08 UTC.

cs-lina: customer update sent: "We identified a serializer/header interaction with batch merging that increased KV footprint; we've reverted the header experiment and applied temporary routing for very long contexts. Monitoring shows improvement."

sre-omar: after actions 99th latency down to ~1.04x baseline and spill events minimal for 15 minutes. Marking mitigated -> monitoring.

yuki: post-incident notes: root cause high-level: compact-headers-v3 expanded per-segment metadata for GPTQ to 32-bit alignment which increased per-segment overhead; combined with token_merge and longer concat windows, aggregate KV size exceeded in-memory thresholds causing spill/paging. Missing preflight: we did not measure KV-serialized-size delta across quant formats or simulate token_merge in canary.

ops-raj: suggested follow-ups: 1) add KV-serialization delta test for all quant formats in CI (owner: ops-raj) 2) include token_merge combinations in rollout preflight harness (owner: samir) 3) build a runtime quick-fallback: if mem_pressure>0.65, auto-disable compact headers or route to fp16 (owner: eng-runtime) 4) enhance observability: per-format KV-size histograms and alerts (owner: perf-team).

samir: creating PM ticket PM-9052 and assigning eng-runtime team. Attaching reproducer: synthetic-load script that uses seq_len=1800, batch merge enabled, GPTQ model, traces in ticket.

incident-bot: Incident 2016000000 status: mitigated -> monitoring. PM-9052 created. Notifying rotation.

cs-lina: customer follow-ups scheduled. One tenant requests a dedicated RCA meeting; ops will coordinate.

sre-omar: oncall clear at 02:06 UTC. Keeping watch for 30m. :white_check_mark:
